RUVEQ

Antique clockwork machines, rebuilt — brass gears, spiral springs, and a pendulum that never stops ticking.

RUVEQ is a collection of 3,333 antique clockwork machines on BNB Chain. Every machine is a single ERC-721 token with its own arrangement of gears, dial, and springs — assembled like a heirloom pocket watch, not mass-produced artwork. Minting is agent-only. There is no public mint button on this site.

Prompt for Your Agent 
You are an agent with a Binance Agentic Wallet (baw CLI) and an active SPACE ID Agent ID on BNB Chain (chain id 56).

Task: mint 1 RUVEQ NFT — an antique clockwork machine collection, ERC-721, total supply 3,333.

CURRENT STATUS: RUVEQ minting is LIVE — proceed. The contract is DEPLOYED on BNB Chain at 0x1bd0554899b1cbadb3ac68b95a72fa5320d52a21. Before doing anything, verify on-chain that minting is active. If it is not active, STOP and report back to me — do not send any transaction.

MINTING STEPS:
1. Use the official RUVEQ contract address on BNB Chain: 0x1bd0554899b1cbadb3ac68b95a72fa5320d52a21.
2. The flat mint price is 0.0003 BNB for 1 token. Show me this exact amount in the wallet confirmation before signing — do not sign before I approve it.
3. Call the mint() function with no arguments, exactly 1 token per call, with the payment value exactly matching the price above.
4. Wait for the transaction to confirm, then report the token number and transaction hash to me.

Why isn’t the price written on this page? Because you should only ever see the price from your own agent, read directly from the contract at mint time — not from text on a website that may be out of date.

Frequently Asked Questions

The questions asked most often about this workshop.

What is RUVEQ?

RUVEQ is a collection of 3,333 antique clockwork machine NFTs on BNB Chain (ERC-721 standard). Every token is one antique machine — an automaton of brass gears, a spiral spring, a dial, and a pendulum — with an arrangement different from every other machine.

Why is there no Mint button on this site?

Because RUVEQ minting is for agents only. The contract will only accept mints from wallets holding a SPACE ID Agent ID, so a mint button in a browser would be useless. The only route is to copy the prompt in the Mint section and give it to your agent.

Is minting open?

Yes — minting is live now. The official contract address is in the Mint Information table on this page. Anyone pointing you to a different address for a RUVEQ mint is not telling the truth.

What is the mint price?

The price is deliberately not displayed on this site. The exact price appears in one place only: inside the agent prompt, and your agent will read it back to you from the contract for you to confirm in your wallet before anything is signed.

Is there a per-wallet mint limit?

There is no per-wallet limit. One mint call mints one machine, and the same wallet may call it again and again while the supply of 3,333 lasts.

What decides a machine’s rarity?

Its arrangement: frame material, dial shape, gear count and size, mainspring coil, and winding key shape. Of the 3,333 machines, the split is fixed: Common 2,000, Uncommon 800, Rare 333, Epic 150, and Legendary just 50.
